plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09): modelling saving for a purchase ('How much do I need to save for it?') and developing a savings plan
plan.shape: short-cycle loops: a savings goal, then saving a fraction or percentage of income, because each adds one step to the last
plan.criticalFeature: weeks needed = amount still needed divided by savings each week, rounded up
decisionPoints: the choice check: weeks to save $95 at $10 a week
the hinge: save 20% of $35 for a $60 goal
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 1? Show one budget: income minus expenses equals money left over.

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it
Weeks = amount still needed divided by savings a week, rounded up

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. A savings goal table, saving a fraction or percentage of pay, a mistake to fix, and planning for a footy jersey.
resources.title: Saving Plans
resources.subtitle: Weeks = amount still needed divided by savings a week, rounded up.

example.prompt: Goal $80. Saved $20. Save $15 a week. How many weeks?

items.prompt: Find how much is still needed and how many weeks it will take.

example.prompt: Earn $40 a week, save 1/4. How much saved a week?

items.prompt: Earn $30 a week. Save 20%. How much a week, and how many weeks to save $90?
Earn $24 a week. Save 3/8. How much a week, and how many weeks to save $100?
items.answer: $9 a week; 100 divided by 9 = 11.1..., so 12 weeks

items.prompt: Ben saves $8 a week for a $50 cap. Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: After 6 weeks he has only $48. He needs 7 weeks: round up when you need the whole amount.

items.explain: $15 a week takes 8 weeks. $25 a fortnight takes 5 fortnights (10 weeks). $50 a month takes 3 months (about 13 weeks).

example.prompt: A $75 jersey. Grandma gives $15. Save $10 a week. Weeks?

items.prompt: Maya wants a $120 footy jersey. She has $27. She earns $18 a week and spends $9.50. How many weeks until she can buy it? Show your plan.
items.answer: Still needed $93. Saves $8.50 a week. 93 divided by 8.5 = 10.9..., so 11 weeks.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Simple interest, a goal that goes on sale, and comparing savings plans, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Interest and Goals
resources.subtitle: Money that grows. Goals that move.

example.prompt: A bank pays 5% a year on $200. Interest after 1 year?

items.prompt: The bank pays 4% of $500 each year (simple interest). Fill in the table.
How many years until the $500 earns $100 in interest?
Another bank pays 6% on $300. Which earns more interest each year: 4% of $500 or 6% of $300?
items.answer: 4% of $500 = $20; 6% of $300 = $18. The first earns more.

example.prompt: Saving $10 a week for a $90 bike. After 4 weeks it goes 20% off. Weeks now?

items.prompt: Ella saves $12 a week for a $150 tablet. After 5 weeks it rises 10%. How many more weeks does she need?
items.answer: Saved $60; new price $165; needs $105; 105 divided by 12 = 8.75, so 9 more weeks

items.prompt: Would you rather save $5 a week or 10% of $45 a week? Explain.
items.answer: 10% of $45 = $4.50, so $5 a week saves more.

example.prompt: Plan to save for a $60 item in 8 weeks.

items.prompt: Choose something you would like to buy (look up or estimate a price). Make a savings plan: how much a week, how many weeks, and what you will give up to save it.
items.answer: Check: a price, a weekly amount, a correct number of weeks (rounded up) and a sensible trade-off.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: savings tables to count up, whole dollars, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Saving: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Count up in your savings each week.

items.prompt: Save $10 a week for $50. Count up: 10, 20, ___. Weeks: ___
Save $8 a week for $40. 40 divided by 8 = ___ weeks

slides.notes: Session 2 of our budgeting week: today we make saving plans.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk; calculators are optional for checking. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with last week's money problems.
ASK: How much change from 20 dollars for 4 drinks at 2.75 each?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $9
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> plan it: cost first, then change. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 4 drinks cost 11 dollars, so the change is 9 dollars.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: taking one drink off.
Fix: reread 4 drinks, and they redo step 1.
notes.prep: Review of last week's financial problems (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Within budget?
prompts: Budget $50. Tickets $18.50 each for 2, plus $12 snacks.

beats: ASK: Is 2 tickets at 18.50 plus 12
dollars of snacks within a 50 dollar budget?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: yes, $49, $1 left
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> add the costs one at a time, then compare with 50. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 37 plus 12 is 49 dollars: within budget,
with 1 dollar left. Tick it or fix it.
trap: adding one ticket.
Fix: reread 2 tickets, and they redo it.

slides.title: Percentage off
prompts: A $45 shirt is reduced to $36. What percentage off?

beats: ASK: What percentage off is a 45 dollar shirt reduced to 36?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 20%
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> find the saving, 9, then 9 out of 45. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 9 dollars off out of 45,
which is one fifth, or 20 percent. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 9%.
Fix: write 9 out of 45 as a fraction,
then a percentage, and they redo it.

beats: SAY: Now for our nine times table.
Write each answer as fast as you can.
ASK: What is 9 times 7?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 63
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 sevens is 70, take one 7 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 63. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 56 or 72.
Fix: 10 sevens is 70, take away 7, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Here's a bigger one.
ASK: What is 9 times 12?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 108
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> 10 twelves is 120, take one 12 away. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 108. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 98 or 118.
Fix: 10 twelves is 120, take away 12, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many nines make 81?
ASK: What is 81 divided by 9?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> count up in nines to 81. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 9. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 8.
Fix: check: 9 nines is 81, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to make a savings plan for something we want to buy.
successCriteria: I can work out how much I still need to save.
I can work out how many weeks it will take to reach a savings goal.
I can compare savings plans and explain which is better.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: Yesterday we found the money left over each week.
Today we use it to plan for something we want.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 still needed is reachable for everyone; SC2 weeks to the goal is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 comparing plans is the stretch.

slides.title: Saving up
slides.prompt: When can Noah buy a $50 skateboard?

beats: POINT along the line.
SAY: Noah saves the same amount each week. This graph shows his total.
ASK: How much does Noah save each week,
and when can he buy a 50 dollar skateboard?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $12 a week; after week 5
SCAN boards for 12 and week 5.
80%+ -> cold call one student: Why not week 4?
Less -> read each point on the line together. Re-ask.
SAY: He saves 12 dollars a week.
After week 4 he has 48, not quite 50,
so he can buy it after week 5. That rounding up is today's big idea.
trap: saying week 4.
Fix: compare 48 with 50, and they look again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: a savings line shows rounding up. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: The amount of money you plan to save, for something you want.
slides.example: My savings goal is $120 for footy boots.

beats: POINT to the words.
SAY: These words are savings goal. Say them with me: sav-ings goal.
SAY: A savings goal is the amount you plan to save, for something you want.
A plan says how much you'll save, and how long it'll take.
ASK: Your goal is $40 and you've saved $15. How much do you still need?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $25
trap: writing $55.
Fix: say you take away what you have, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Still needed = goal minus already saved.

slides.title: Weeks to the goal
steps: Save $12 a week: 80 divided by 12 = 6 r 8.

beats: MODEL still needed.
SAY: The goal is 95 dollars and I've saved 15, so I still need 80.
MODEL dividing and rounding.
SAY: At 12 dollars a week, 80 divided by 12 is 6, remainder 8.
After 6 weeks I'd have 87, still short, so I need 7 weeks.
ASK: Goal $70, saved $10, save $8 a week. How many weeks?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 8 weeks
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Still need 60. 60 divided by 8 is 7, remainder 4, so 8 weeks.
trap: rounding down to 7.
Fix: check 7 lots of 8 against 60, and they round up.
notes.stretch: How much would you need to save a week to do it in 5 weeks?
notes.help: Count up in your weekly savings in a table.
notes.prep: Still needed, divide, round up: the critical feature. SC1 and SC2.

beats: MODEL finding the saving.
SAY: If I earn 40 dollars a week and save 25 percent,
I save a quarter: 10 dollars.
MODEL the weeks.
SAY: For a 65 dollar goal, 65 divided by 10 is 6.5,
so I round up to 7 weeks.
ASK: Earn $30 a week and save 20%.
How much a week, and how many weeks for $50?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $6 a week, 9 weeks
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 20 percent of 30 is 6 dollars.
50 divided by 6 is 8.3, so 9 weeks.
trap: dividing 50 by 30.
Fix: find the weekly saving first, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: What percentage would you need to save to do it in 5 weeks?
notes.prep: Two steps: the saving, then the weeks. SC2.

slides.title: How many weeks?
slides.prompt: Save $10 a week for $95. Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: leaves a part week instead of whole weeks

beats: SAY: Think about whether you have enough at the end of each week.
ASK: How many weeks to save 95 dollars at 10 dollars a week?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Why not 9?
Less -> count up in tens together: 10, 20... 90, 100. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B. After 9 weeks there's only 90,
so we need a 10th week to reach 95.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: count up to week 9, 90 dollars, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point: rounding up in a savings context.

slides.title: Saving plans
slides.ask: How many weeks will it take?
slides.pivot: find still needed, divide, then round up
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Did you round up? Why?

items.say: 85 divided by 15 is 5 r 10, so round up to 6 weeks.
10 percent is 5 a week. 32 divided by 5 is 6.4: 7 weeks.

say: Write the number of weeks on your board.
trap: rounding down.
Fix: check the total at that week against the goal, and they round up.
notes.stretch: Write the total saved at the end of each plan.
notes.help: Count up your savings in a table.
notes.prep: Guided practice: exact, with savings already, a remainder, and a percentage of pay. SC2.

visual.text: Zac earns $35 a week and saves 20%. His goal is $60.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Find the weekly saving first.
ASK: How many weeks until Zac reaches his 60 dollar goal?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9 weeks
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> find 20 percent of 35 together, then divide and round. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 20 percent of 35 is 7 dollars.
60 divided by 7 is 8 r 4,
so 9 weeks. Tick it or fix it.
trap: dividing 60 by 35.
Fix: find the weekly saving first, and they redo it.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone with 8 weeks or 2 weeks starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Make and check saving plans on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Did you round up? How do you know?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: rounding down.
Fix: check the total at that week, and they round up.
notes.stretch: Extension: simple interest, goals that move, and your own plan.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: savings tables to count up, whole dollars.
notes.prep: Independent practice: a goal table, saving part of pay, a mistake and a jersey plan. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: When will Priya reach her goal? Show your plan.

visual.text: Priya wants $110 for a netball. She has $22 and puts away $9 every week.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: After how many weeks can Priya buy the netball?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 10 weeks
RECORD who forgets what is saved or rounds down.
They start tomorrow's spreadsheet work with the teacher.
trap: writing 9 or 12.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: still needed, divide, round up.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner why we round up when saving.

notes.answer: open - listen for rounding down leaves you short of the goal
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can make a savings plan?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with 9 on the board matters most.
ASK: Why do we round up the weeks when saving?
20 sec. Cue: Partner B first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: rounding down leaves you short of the goal
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: budgets in a spreadsheet.
